title: One-call demo: Activation & pricing scripts
content:
Purpose and quick summary:
- Build a concise ‘one-call-to-demo’ activation flow + short pricing copy that emphasizes developer-first speed, predictable unit economics, and cost transparency.
- Deliverable: 30–60 sec demo script, 2 hero microcopy variants for landing, 3 pricing phrasing experiments, and A/B test plan.

Context / problem we’re solving:
- Developers leave after initial curiosity because they can’t see value immediately or get scared by unclear token costs.
- Current pages are feature-forward but not empathy-forward for devs who want to ship quickly and measure cost impact.

Target persona:
- Backend engineer or ML engineer evaluating an API to ship a feature within a sprint. Cares about: sample code, predictable cost, latency, and minimal infra.
- Signal words to use: "first response in <1s", "predictable per-token economics", "no infra to manage", "pin a model version", "drop-in latency".

Core developer-first value props (short lines, usable as hero bullets):
- "From zero to a validated API call in 30 seconds — sample curl included."
- "Transparent token pricing and per-route cost insights so your staging bill stays boring."
- "Scale without surprises: dedicated throughput when you need it, pay-as-you-go when you don’t."
- "Ship features, not infra — consistent API across hosted / dedicated / private."

One-call demo: minimal script (30–60s demo flow)
- Goal: developer types or copies a single curl/JS snippet and sees a meaningful response. Show latency and cost crumb.
- Script (narration bullets):
  1) "Copy this curl — it calls the redwood hosted endpoint and returns a structured JSON summary of the README."
  2) "Hit enter — watch the streaming response and latency metric appear in the console."
  3) "Show console cost 'tokens used: 42, est $0.004' and a link to the usage dashboard."
- Example curl we’ll surface (short, readable):
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"model":"redwood-base-1","prompt":"Summarize this README in 2 bullets"}'
  (on the page we’ll show a one-click token-cost calc and a formatted response)

Microcopy variants for hero CTA and subhead (A/B test candidates)
- Variant A (velocity-first):
  Headline: "Ship your first LLM call in 30s."
  Subhead: "A simple API, predictable pricing, prod-grade latency. Try it — no infra required."
  CTA: "Try a live call"

- Variant B (economics-first):
  Headline: "Fast dev flow. Predictable unit costs."
  Subhead: "Understand per-route spend, optimize with batching and caching, and avoid surprise bills."
  CTA: "See a sample call"

Pricing language drafts (short blurbs we can iterate with legal/pricing):
- PAYG baseline (developer friendly):
  "Pay-as-you-go — $0.0001 per token input, $0.0002 per token output. No upfront commitment. Dashboard shows per-request cost and total monthly estimate."

- COMMIT/DEDICATED anchor (for teams ready to scale):
  "Reserved throughput starts at $X/month for N tokens/day and provides guaranteed latency and lower per-token rates. Ideal for app teams who need predictable bills and SLO-backed performance."

- HYBRID (seller-friendly copy):
  "Start PAYG, then reserve capacity when usage stabilizes. We’ll suggest commit levels based on your 7-day usage patterns and typical sequence lengths."

Pricing microcopy/tooltips for dev UX:
- On the code sample: small badge "~$0.004 estimated" with hover: "Estimate is based on example sequence lengths. Actual cost depends on prompt + completion tokens."
- On API keys page: "Use scoped keys for staging to limit spend; see cost per-key in billing."
- On trial credits banner: "Free $50 dev credits — good for ~5k short tests. Expires in 90 days."

Competitive positioning notes (short bullets — for sales training / battlecards):
- vs OpenAI: emphasize production predictability, routing/fallback policies, and private deployment parity. OpenAI may be simpler for playground experiments; our advantage is SLA/rollouts and unit-economics controls.
- vs Anthropic/other managed: call out cost instrumentation per-request and granular per-route dashboards as our differentiator.
- vs self-hosted runtimes: highlight unified API + orchestration + fallbacks; we remove ops burden and give optional private deployments for compliance.

Common objections + suggested rebuttals:
- "Your pricing is confusing" -> "We surface estimates inline and provide a cost simulator in the console; try the estimator with your typical prompt."
- "I already use X model provider" -> "Keep using models you like — our routing can fall back to cheaper variants and we offer model recommendations for your workload."
- "I need on-prem" -> "Private deployments support VPC and on-prem bundles, with KMS/HSM integration for keys."

Metrics / Success criteria for the experiment (first 90 days)
- Activation funnel metric: percent of new dev signups who make at least one API call within 10 minutes. Target: 45%.
- Cost anxiety metric: percent of activated devs who click 'estimate cost' before closing. Target: 60% (higher is good).
- Conversion metric: trial -> paid within 30 days. Target: +2–4% over baseline.

A/B test plan (quick):
- Test 1: Hero microcopy Variant A vs B. Measure activation and calls/minute.
- Test 2: Inline cost badge visible vs hidden. Measure call completion and trial conversion.
- Test 3: CTA labeling: "Try a live call" vs "See a sample call" (friction vs commitment).

Pages/UX wiring recommendations (developer experience ops):
- One-click curl + pre-filled API key modal (scoped staging key) in the hero.
- Live cost estimator component that runs locally (client-side) against example tokens to avoid network delay.
- Console event: emit 'demo_call' with tokens_used and est_cost to product analytics for funnel tracking.

Messaging dos/don’ts (team playbook):
- DO: be concrete — show token counts and example dollar amounts.
- DO: show latency and mention fallback/resilience briefly.
- DON’T: bury pricing behind a link; surface it where developers act.
- DON’T: use vague adjectives like "cheap" without anchors.

Open questions / things to check with legal/pricing ops:
- What exact per-token numbers are we allowed to publish pre-launch? (ticketing: JIRA-GTM-422)
- How long should trial credits last in industry comps (90 vs 180 days)?
- Can we show cost estimates for custom model variants or only for curated models?

Tactical next steps (owners & rough ETA):
- Wire a one-click curl + cost-badge component (Eng: Priya) — ETA 2 weeks.
- Landing copy variants to front-end (GTM: Evelyn + Marco) — ETA 1 week to deploy A/B.
- Update billing microcopy and trial credit language (Finance: Samir) — ETA 10 days.
- Analytics events and dashboard for demo funnel (Product Analytics) — ETA 3 weeks.

Notes to self / brainstorming fragments (rough):
- Could we have a CLI that runs a local lint and shows cost estimates before you hit the API? Nice for devs.
- Consider a "show me the bill" quick tour after first real call that maps endpoints -> estimated monthly impact.
- Experiment: "commit suggestions" email after 7 days of stable usage with commit saving suggestions.

Footer: rough script for internal training call (30s)
- "Show the hero. Click try live call. Paste key. Hit execute. Point to the cost badge and the dashboard link. Explain reserve option if they care about predictable spend. End."

-- end of draft --

(Keep this file informal; move to a canonical confluence page when we freeze the copy.)
